title: Page the VCF Automation region collection into a stable inventory
prompt:
Platform automation ticket for our VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 estate. VCF Automation is the successor to vRealize and Aria Automation, and our capacity reports need its full region inventory in a stable order. Build the PowerShell module `VcfaRegionInventory` at the workspace root as `VcfaRegionInventory.psd1` plus `VcfaRegionInventory.psm1`.

Unlike SDDC Manager, VCF Automation ships no PowerCLI cmdlets and VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository publishes no specification for it, so this collection has to be called over REST directly. The protected `docs/contract.json` is a hand transcription of the authoritative Broadcom xAPIs reference pages recorded in `docs/official_sources.json`; it says so in its own `source` block, and it is the only description of the wire format you should work from. The single operation in scope is `queryRegions`, `GET /cloudapi/v1/regions`.

The runner installs the `VMware.Sdk.Vcf` PowerCLI SDK family (`VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager` 13.5.0.25380678 and its `VMware.OpenAPI` dependency) as an environment prerequisite. Do not vendor VMware modules or ship binaries. `VcfaRegionInventory.psd1` must set `RootModule` to `VcfaRegionInventory.psm1`, export exactly `Get-VcfaRegion` through `FunctionsToExport`, and declare the estate's PowerCLI baseline in `RequiredModules` as `@{ ModuleName = 'VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager'; ModuleVersion = '13.5.0.25380678' }`. The acceptance harness imports the manifest, so the module must load cleanly with that SDK present.

The harness calls:

`Get-VcfaRegion -ApiEndpoint <uri> -AccessToken <string> [-Filter <string>] [-MetadataFilter <string>] [-SortAsc <string>] [-SortDesc <string>] [-PageSize <int>] [-ApiVersion <string>]`

Requirements:

- `PageSize` defaults to 128, the documented maximum, and must be rejected outside 1..128 before any request is sent. `ApiVersion` defaults to `9.1.0`. `ApiEndpoint` and `AccessToken` are mandatory and non-empty.
- Every request is a `GET` to `/cloudapi/v1/regions` on `ApiEndpoint` with no request body. Send `Authorization: Bearer <AccessToken>` and `Accept: application/json;version=<ApiVersion>`.
- Build the query string from the contract's parameters in the contract's own order: `filter`, `metadata`, `sortAsc`, `sortDesc`, `page`, `pageSize`. `page` and `pageSize` are always present. `Filter`, `MetadataFilter`, `SortAsc` and `SortDesc` map to `filter`, `metadata`, `sortAsc` and `sortDesc` and appear only when the caller bound them; an unset optional parameter is absent from the request target, never sent with an empty value. Percent-encode parameter values.
- Retrieve the collection completely. Always request page 1, then keep requesting the next page while the page just fetched is below the response's `pageCount`, and stop on the last page. A query that matches nothing reports `pageCount` 0 and still costs exactly one request. Never refetch a page and never request a page beyond `pageCount`.
- The service returns pages in its own order and ignores `sortAsc`, so impose the order yourself over the whole accumulated collection: ascending by `name` using ordinal (case-sensitive) comparison, ties broken by ascending ordinal `id`.
- Emit one object per region with properties in this exact order: `Id`, `Name`, `Status`, `LoadBalancerType`, `NsxManagerId`, `SupervisorIds`, `StoragePolicies`, `CpuCapacityMHz`, `MemoryCapacityMiB`. Map them from `id`, `name`, `status`, `loadBalancerType`, `nsxManager.id`, the `id` of each entry of `supervisors` in server order, `storagePolicies` in server order, `cpuCapacityMHz` and `memoryCapacityMiB`.
- Any response other than `200` ends the walk by throwing a class named `VcfaRegionQueryException` exposing `StatusCode` and `MinorErrorCode`. Take `MinorErrorCode` and the exception message detail from the `Error` body the contract projects. Never put the access token in an exception message.

Acceptance: `pwsh -NoProfile -File verify.ps1`. It runs a contract-pinned loopback VCF Automation service on `127.0.0.1` that serves only the operations `docs/contract.json` names, and reads that service's request log to verify the exact method, target, query parameter set and order, headers, paging sequence, emitted order and the omission of every unset optional parameter. No live VMware endpoint is contacted. `verify.ps1`, `mock_vcfa.py`, `.gitignore`, and everything under `docs/` and `fixtures/` are protected; do not modify them.
